beats.intro: Chapter eight, lesson four. {{ATP|A T P}} and energy coupling. [[battery]]A rechargeable battery stores energy, spends it, and gets charged again. [[cells]]Inside a cell, something very like that is going on all the time. [[strip]]Here is our pathway strip again. Some of its steps run uphill, and they will not go on their own. [[spark]]This lesson is about the spark that gives them a push. [[work]]A cell does three main kinds of work. [[chem]]Chemical work builds molecules. [[trans]]Transport work moves substances across membranes. [[mech]]Mechanical work moves things, like a vesicle on its track. [[need]]All three are endergonic, so they need energy. [[coupling]]To pay for them, cells use energy coupling: an exergonic process drives an endergonic one. [[byatp]]And most energy coupling in cells is done by {{ATP|A T P}}.
beats.atp: [[atp]]{{ATP|A T P}}, adenosine triphosphate, is the cell's energy shuttle. [[parts]]It has three parts. [[aden]]Adenine, a nitrogenous base. [[ribo]]Ribose, a five-carbon sugar. [[nosine]]Together, those two make adenosine. [[phos]]And a tail of three phosphate groups. [[tri]]Tri-phosphate means three phosphates. [[tail]]Each phosphate carries a negative charge, and like charges push each other apart. So the three are crowded together in the tail, like springs pressed tight.
beats.hydro: [[water]]Add water, and the end phosphate can be broken off. That is hydrolysis. [[split]]{{ATP|A T P}} plus water gives {{ADP|A D P}}, adenosine diphosphate, which has two phosphates, [[pi]]plus one free inorganic phosphate. [[drop]]Energy is released, about minus seven point three kilocalories per mole. Now be careful about where that energy comes from. [[notbond]]It does not come from the phosphate bonds themselves. [[lower]]It comes from the change to a state of lower free energy. [[ball]]The products are more stable than {{ATP|A T P}} was, like a ball that has rolled downhill. [[height]]The energy is the difference in height.
beats.q1: Quick check. Where does the energy of {{ATP|A T P}} hydrolysis come from?
beats.couple: [[glu]]Now a worked example. Turning glutamic acid and ammonia into glutamine is endergonic. Delta G is plus three point four kilocalories per mole, [[alone]]so on its own it will not go. [[atpjoin]]But {{ATP|A T P}} hydrolysis is exergonic, minus seven point three. [[step1]]Step one. {{ATP|A T P}} transfers a phosphate group to glutamic acid. That is phosphorylation, and the glutamic acid is now a phosphorylated intermediate. It is less stable, and more reactive, than before. {{ADP|A D P}} leaves. [[step2]]Step two. Ammonia replaces the phosphate, which leaves as inorganic phosphate, and glutamine is made. [[net]]Add the two energies. [[sum]]Plus three point four, and minus seven point three, give a net delta G of minus three point nine. [[overall]]Overall, the coupled reaction is exergonic, so it goes.
beats.movers: [[transport]]Transport work. {{ATP|A T P}} phosphorylates a transport protein. [[pg]]The phosphate group changes the protein's shape, and that moves the solute across the membrane. [[off]]Then the phosphate comes off as inorganic phosphate. [[motor]]Mechanical work. {{ATP|A T P}} binds to a motor protein and is hydrolysed. [[walks]]The motor changes shape and walks a vesicle along its cytoskeletal track. [[same]]Chemical, transport and mechanical. [[fuel]]Three kinds of work, and one fuel. [[each]]In each one, an endergonic job is paid for by the exergonic hydrolysis of {{ATP|A T P}}.
beats.q2: Quick check. Is each one exergonic, or endergonic?
beats.cycle: [[renew]]{{ATP|A T P}} is a renewable resource. [[regen]]Adding a phosphate group back onto {{ADP|A D P}} rebuilds it, [[catab]]and the energy for that comes from catabolic reactions in the cell. [[door]]So the {{ATP|A T P}} cycle is a revolving door. Energy from catabolism comes in, [[workout]]and energy for cellular work goes out. [[fast]]A busy cell turns over its {{ATP|A T P}} again and again, millions of times every second. [[end]]To sum up. [[s1]]{{ATP|A T P}} hydrolysis is exergonic. [[s2]]Coupling uses that energy, often through a phosphorylated intermediate, to drive endergonic work. [[s3]]And catabolism recharges the {{ADP|A D P}}. Now try the practice.
